answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks in AI agent economies, networks mandate hardware-attested cryptographic stake where each agent executes within a secure enclave built on a unique ferrous substrate. Agents emit a zero-knowledge whisper of execution proofs across a distributed grove of validator nodes. This mechanism forces attackers to incur non-trivial physical hardware acquisition costs rather than negligible virtual instantiation costs, making large-scale identity cloning economically unviable.
